clue.text: Check for one out of steam?

indicators.note: taken out of signals that one letter is removed from the word steam

parts.note: one is A, as in 'a' meaning a single thing

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a check is needed for a machine that has run out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For one' looks like 'for example', but 'one' is A, and 'out of' takes that A away from STEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to check or halt it.

clue.text: Sage chopped for a very long time

indicators.note: herbs that are chopped are cut up and jumbled, so the letters of the herb are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook has been chopping sage for what feels like forever.
explanation.definitionFit: 'For ages' is the everyday idiom for an extremely long stretch of time.

clue.text: Indiscreet outbreak

explanation.surface: An indiscreet remark breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: A hasty, careless act is rash, and an outbreak of spots on the skin is also a rash.

clue.text: Girl proud of her digital display?

definitions.text: Girl proud of her digital display?

parts.words: Girl proud of her digital display?
parts.note: the digital display is a ring worn on a finger, a digit, which a newly engaged woman shows off

explanation.surface: A girl shows off something on a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests electronics, but a digit is a finger, and the display is an engagement ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman engaged to be married wears a new ring and is proud to show it.

clue.text: Performance in which the middle section is agitated

definitions.text: Performance in which the middle section is agitated

parts.words: Performance in which the middle section is agitated
parts.note: the middle section is the dancer's midriff, which is shaken in an oriental dance, rather than the middle part of a concert

explanation.surface: A concert in which the central movement is frantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle section' suggests a movement of a piece of music; it is the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: In this Middle Eastern dance the performer rolls and shakes the stomach.

clue.text: All-male race-that gets us nowhere

parts.note: a stag party or stag night is for men only
a race or people can be called a nation

explanation.surface: A men-only race that goes nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is a state of no progress or movement.

clue.text: As much as a sewer can take

definitions.text: As much as a sewer can take

parts.words: As much as a sewer can take
parts.note: a sewer here is someone who sews, not a drain, and the amount is the thread that one threading takes

explanation.surface: How much a drain can cope with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' reads as a drain; it is a person sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the length of thread put through the eye at one time for stitching.

clue.text: Vegetable providing general potassium requirement

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A vegetable said to meet a general's potassium needs.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a long white onion-family vegetable, the national emblem of Wales.

clue.text: Washed-out retrograde deal to include subordinate

indicators.note: to include means the reversed word holds the other piece inside it
retrograde means moving backwards, so the word deal is read in reverse

parts.note: a subordinate is under someone

explanation.surface: A faded, backward-looking deal that brings in a junior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrograde' turns DEAL into LAED, and 'to include' puts UNDER inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundered clothes have been cleaned in the wash.

clue.text: Mechanics involved in accident

indicators.note: involved suggests something tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Mechanics are caught up in a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischance is a piece of bad luck, an unlucky accident.

clue.text: Potter's implement

parts.note: a potter here is a snooker or billiards player who pots balls, not a maker of ceramics

explanation.surface: A tool used by someone making pots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' suggests clay; in snooker, a potter sends balls into pockets with a long stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The tapered stick used to strike balls in snooker and billiards.

clue.text: No peach, we hear, this hybrid fruit

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a peach is a beauty, so someone who is no peach is plain-looking

explanation.surface: Someone notes that this cross-bred fruit is not a peach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peach' looks like the fruit, but here it means a beautiful person.
explanation.definitionFit: This Jamaican fruit is a cross between a grapefruit and a tangerine.

clue.text: Leo's retreat is a squalid room

explanation.surface: The lion's hideaway is a filthy room.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is the lion, whose lair is its den; a den is also a dirty, seedy room.

clue.text: Career fit for Veronica?

parts.note: to career is to rush along, so career as a noun is rapid speed
fit in health means well

explanation.surface: Is a career suitable for a woman named Veronica?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Veronica' looks like a woman's name; it is the botanical genus of the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is the Latin genus name of this small blue-flowered plant.

clue.text: Dachshund on the trail of the banger

parts.note: banger is British slang for a sausage
to dog someone is to follow on their trail

explanation.surface: A small dog hunts down a firework.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a sausage as well as a firework; 'on the trail of' is the verb for following, put after the banger in answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the popular nickname for the dachshund, from its sausage-like body.

clue.text: A voice not altered in calling up

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters of the phrase are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A voice that does not change when it phones someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Evocation is the summoning of a memory or spirit into the mind.

clue.text: Bark-lined construction fit for swallows

indicators.note: construction means building something up from parts, so the letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A nest lined with bark makes a fine home for swallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallows' are birds in the surface; here they are gulps.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drinkable is fit to be swallowed as a drink.

clue.text: Bird dead, with nothing to follow-you can say that again!

indicators.note: the phrase literally asks for the same pair of letters to be said a second time
to follow means the next piece comes after the first

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for dead, as on family trees
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A bird drops dead with nothing after it, and someone heartily agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You can say that again' sounds like agreement but tells you to repeat DO.
explanation.definitionFit: This extinct flightless bird of Mauritius is a byword for something long gone.

clue.text: British union-leaders with belly-ache coming from the country

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of the two words before it

parts.note: colic is a severe stomach pain

explanation.surface: Heads of a British trade union complain of stomach pains on returning from the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucolic means rural or pastoral, relating to country life.

clue.text: Slight but deliberate insult

explanation.surface: An insult that is minor but intended.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight is a snub, and an affront is an intentional offence.

clue.text: Place to which painter is atta ehed?

definitions.text: Place to which painter is atta ehed?

parts.words: Place to which painter is atta ehed?
parts.note: a painter here is the rope at a boat's bow used to tie it up, not an artist, and this is where it is made fast

explanation.surface: An artist's studio or favourite haunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter' suggests an artist; on a boat it is the line that ties it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A berth or spot where a boat is tied up is where it is moored.

clue.text: Long story is a delightful thing whenretiring

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: a gas is informal for something great fun

explanation.surface: Hearing a long tale is a pleasure at bedtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a lengthy narrative, originally an Old Norse tale.

clue.text: Wisdom of having long week ar arranged with extra day

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The good sense of planning a long week with a bonus day.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning and understanding gathered over time amount to wisdom.

clue.text: Charles' mother

parts.note: Charles here is the essayist Charles Lamb, and a lamb's mother is a female sheep

explanation.surface: The mother of a man called Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious Charles is royal; this one is the writer Charles Lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamb's mother is a female sheep.

clue.text: Drink for some sedate after noon parties

definitions.text: Drink for some sedate after noon parties

indicators.note: some of means only a part of the words is used, a run within them

explanation.surface: A drink for genteel parties held in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes a run of letters across 'sedaTE After', while the whole clue also describes the drink served at afternoon gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a hot drink made by infusing leaves.

clue.text: Kind of house from the home counties, next to motorway

indicators.note: next to means the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A type of house in the commuter belt beside a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in South East England.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi is a semi-detached house sharing one wall with its neighbour.

clue.text: Tapped daily in lobby, one feels the pressure

definitions.text: Tapped daily in lobby, one feels the pressure

parts.words: Tapped daily in lobby, one feels the pressure
parts.note: an instrument hanging in a hallway is tapped each day to read air pressure, rather than a stressed person being bugged

explanation.surface: A lobbyist under pressure has their phone tapped daily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tapped' suggests phone bugging; people tap a hall weather-glass to free its needle.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument measures atmospheric pressure to forecast weather.

clue.text: Word of the French taken by Henry the first, a fly-by-night

indicators.note: taken by means the first piece picks up the next one

parts.note: mot is French for word

indicators.note: the first picks out the opening letter of the name Henry

explanation.surface: A French word adopted by King Henry I describes a shady character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry the first' looks like the king; it means the first letter of Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly-by-night is something that flies at night, as this insect does.

clue.text: River drivers start from?

explanation.surface: Where motorists set off near a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tees is a river in north-east England, and golfers hit drives from little pegs on the tee.

clue.text: eg. Derby or Redcar's first champion

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of Redcar

parts.note: an ace is an expert or champion

explanation.surface: The Derby or the leading winner at Redcar racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is a famous horse race; Redcar is an English racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby is an example of a horse race.

clue.text: Depressed county

explanation.surface: A county in low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low is feeling down, and Down is a county of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: A bit short of the right amount?

definitions.text: A bit short of the right amount?

parts.words: A bit short of the right amount?
parts.note: the British phrase right as ninepence makes ninepence the right amount, and a coin value one penny less falls just short

explanation.surface: Someone has been slightly short-changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right as ninepence' is an old British saying for perfectly fine; a 'bit' was also slang for a small coin.
explanation.definitionFit: One penny less than ninepence, the sum in the old British saying for being all right.
